# GEO report: quay-store

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

Everything below is read from code. I didn't run a live check, and Bash was denied during the audit, so I read the files directly. This is a SvelteKit app with 3 routes (`/`, `/shop`, `/search`). I read all of them, along with `static/robots.txt` and `static/sitemap.xml`. There is no `geo.config.json`.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. A cap of 40 applies because GEO-009 has a blocker: Googlebot is blocked from the whole site (`static/robots.txt:5`). Both numbers are therefore limited to 40.

In plain terms, the site is told to keep Google out entirely, and its pages are built in the browser, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript see an empty page. Nothing is left unknown, so the range is a single number. I assumed you want to be found, because there is no policy file saying otherwise.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Stop blocking Googlebot in robots.txt
- **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` for Googlebot tells Google not to read any page. That also makes your sitemap and indexable pages (`/`, `/shop`) contradict each other (GEO-009 and GEO-014).
- **Where:** `static/robots.txt:4-5`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: Googlebot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 72/100, Good (earned 18 ÷ 25). The cap is lifted. If the block is intended, change your declared policy instead.

### 2. Render the pages on the server
- **Why it matters:** Many crawlers read only the first HTML and don't run JavaScript. With server rendering off, they get an empty shell instead of your headings and text (GEO-003). Note that the nav links also exist only after JavaScript runs.
- **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** Alone, 60 raw, which is still capped at 40 until item 1 is done. After items 1 and 2, 84/100, Good.

### 3. Set the page language and fill in descriptions
- **Why it matters:** Without `lang`, machines have to guess your language. `/shop` has an empty description, and `/search` has none (GEO-012).
- **Where:** `src/app.html:2` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3`
- **What the code says:** `<html>` and `<meta name="description" content="" />`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** Alone, 56 raw, which is still capped at 40 until item 1 is done. After items 1, 2 and 3, 92/100, Strong.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `static/robots.txt`, small plain text with valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Problem | Not run | `static/robots.txt:4-5` blocks Googlebot site-wide. `*` is allowed. |
| GEO-014 | Sitemap-listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/shop` are both blocked for Googlebot by `static/robots.txt:5` (0 of 2 routes clear). `/search` is intentionally noindex (`src/routes/search/+page.svelte:3`), is unlinked and is not in the sitemap, so it is fine. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+page.svelte:4`, `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:4`. Both use `https://quay.example`, matching the sitemap and robots. |
| GEO-003 | Primary content is in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`, `ssr = false` (all 3 routes affected) |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and meets requirements | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`. The JSON is valid, but the Product has only `name` and no `offers`, `review` or `aggregateRating` (0 of 1 route clear). |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Clear | Not run | `static/sitemap.xml` is a valid urlset. `static/robots.txt:7` has an absolute `Sitemap:` line. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | Not run | `src/app.html:2` has no `lang` (site-wide). `/shop` has an empty description (`src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3`). |
| GEO-016 | Key routes reachable through links | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5` links to `/` and `/shop` with `<a href>`. |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:7` uses only the scoped `data-nosnippet`. I found no page-wide `nosnippet` and no header-setting code. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | I read the layout and 3 pages: no images, links have text, every page has a title. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared. |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` found. This isn't a problem. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. |

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Headers and status codes:** real status codes, redirects and any `X-Robots-Tag` header set at hosting level aren't visible in the repository. A live scan would confirm them.
- **Training crawlers:** `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` have no rules in `robots.txt`, so they are allowed. This is your choice and isn't scored.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, since there is no `geo.config.json`.
- `https://quay.example` is the real origin. It is consistent across the canonicals, sitemap and robots.txt, but it looks like a placeholder.
- `/search` is meant to stay out of search results.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
